_what_this_figure_is: A licensing diagram, not a result. It draws the asymmetry between what the probe positive licenses and what a negative would have licensed. It has no axis of any measured quantity, no plotted value, no bar, no interval and no marker on a scale. Its one axis is depth, and depth is an index, not a measurement. PASS 14: after this pass the asymmetry is legible three ways -- in the strike, which eliminates one branch of a two-member partition; in the two licence columns, where (c) sets 39 characters against (d) 58 and the second row is the whole of the difference (a negative names one of the seven depths on the axis, the positive names none); and in the caption, which carries the fix classes and the premise they depend on.
_intervals: None. The probe returns a cross-validated accuracy and RESULTS_cluster/workspace_probe.json stores no interval for it. Nothing in this figure is a bar, a whisker or a dot on a rule, so nothing invites one. Same rule as comparators.tex and style_v2.py: intervals are drawn only where the instrument returns the document convention. PASS 12 stated this ON THE DRAWING for the first time, in one \scriptsize quietink line at the figure foot. PASS 14 the line reads "Nothing here is an estimate; the seven depth ticks are the only scaled marks." -- 76 characters, 9.60cm, one line, left-aligned to the figure x origin at x = 0.00, baseline y = 0.38. Pass 13 second clause, "the counts are the probe design", is deleted: pass 13 made TWO changes at once and it was the other one -- "a measured quantity" becoming "an estimate" -- that removed the contradiction pass 12 wording had with the 480/twelve/forty line beneath it, since a count is not an estimate. The clause was belt and braces, 35 characters, inside the longest string in a figure over its S15 ink ceiling. The word "seven", which pass 12 deleted with the caret label and pass 13 restored, is still here.
_what_may_not_be_read_off_this_figure: The prompt strip has NO horizontal scale and no token count. Cell widths are set from the measured typeset width of each field name and nothing else. The control cell's sentence is by far the longest field in a real prompt and is not drawn longer.
The depth axis is the only scaled mark. Its scale is layer index, not accuracy: nothing in the figure varies with a measured quantity.

the_strike.weight_and_colour_repaired_pass_13: THIS IS THE HIGHEST-PRIORITY REPAIR IN THIS FIGURE, and it is a correctness defect rather than a preference. Black solid 0.90pt is the register S6 and CF2 reserve, across the whole slate, for a THRESHOLD: chance in 4.11(a), the removal gate in 4.9, the 10% pre-registered materiality margin in 4.12 and 4.13, and style_v2.chance_line()'s own hard-coded color='black', lw=0.9, solid. S6's check is not 'no collision here' but 'nothing that is not a threshold may be black solid 0.9pt', and pass 12's defence (this figure contains no threshold, so nothing collides) answers S10's singleton clause and not S6's. This figure prints six pages before the reader meets the first real threshold in the arc and is the first figure of the slate, so it was teaching the threshold stroke on a negation. Measured on the pass-12 render, the strikes were grey 25 (ink) over grey 107 (quietink) text, i.e. the branch the chapter DISCARDS carried the darkest ink on the page while the branch the chapter measures receded -- the S8 inversion C3 fixed in colour, reintroduced in weight, and the squint render resolved the dead branch first. Both strikes are now quietink 0.40pt, the colour and weight of the text they cross. 0.40pt was already live in this figure (the axis rule, the drug cell's border), so no new register appears and no singleton is created; 0.50pt was rejected because S10 reserves it for a dotted coordinate; quietink 0.90pt was rejected because 0.90pt is the slate's threshold weight whatever its colour, and because a 0.90pt rule through \scriptsize text does not survive at print size.
